BUG REPORT: When a proxy load balancer has no targets, `Next` panics instead of returning nil:
- `NewRandomBalancer(nil).Next(c)` panics with `panic: invalid argument to Intn`
- `NewRoundRobinBalancer([]*ProxyTarget{}).Next(c)` panics with `panic: runtime error: integer divide by zero`
Expected behavior: `Next` must return `nil` when the target list is empty, so callers can handle "no target available".

REQUIRED EDITS in /echo/middleware/proxy.go:

1) `randomBalancer.Next` must become:

```go
// Next randomly returns an upstream target.
func (b *randomBalancer) Next(c echo.Context) *ProxyTarget {
	if b.random == nil {
		b.random = rand.New(rand.NewSource(int64(time.Now().Nanosecond())))
	}
	b.mutex.RLock()
	defer b.mutex.RUnlock()
	if len(b.targets) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return b.targets[b.random.Intn(len(b.targets))]
}
```

2) `roundRobinBalancer.Next` must become:

```go
// Next returns an upstream target using round-robin technique.
func (b *roundRobinBalancer) Next(c echo.Context) *ProxyTarget {
	b.mutex.RLock()
	defer b.mutex.RUnlock()
	if len(b.targets) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	b.i = b.i % uint32(len(b.targets))
	t := b.targets[b.i]
	atomic.AddUint32(&b.i, 1)
	return t
}
```

ROOT CAUSE: in /echo/router.go, `func (r *Router) Find(method, path string, c Context)` starts with:

```go
	ctx := c.(*context)
	ctx.path = path
	currentNode := r.tree // Current node as root
```

The first assignment makes `ctx.path` the raw request path for every request, including ones that never match a route (Find returns early in that case and never reaches the line `ctx.path = currentNode.ppath` near the end of Find).

REQUIRED EDIT: delete exactly the line `	ctx.path = path` from `Router.Find` in /echo/router.go, so that `ctx.path` is only ever set to the matched node's pristine route path (`ctx.path = currentNode.ppath`). BUG: registering two route groups with the same prefix, each with its own middleware, makes the first group's routes 404:

```go
e := echo.New()
g1 := e.Group("/group", m1)
g1.GET("", h)
g2 := e.Group("/group", m2)
g2.GET("/other", h)
```

`GET /group` returns 404 even though it is registered; only the second group works. Expected: `GET /group` runs `h` with `m1`; `GET /group/other` runs `h` with `m2`.

ROOT CAUSE: `Group.Use` (group.go) registers catch-all routes `g.Any("", NotFoundHandler)` and `g.Any("/*", NotFoundHandler)` so that group middleware runs for unmatched requests. `Any` registers the NotFoundHandler for every HTTP method, so the second group's `Use` overwrites the first group's real `GET /group` handler.

FIX (this mirrors the upstream design): introduce a special pseudo-method `RouteNotFound` used only as a fallback when no handler exists for the request method.

1) /echo/echo.go — add this exported constant near the other top-level constants (e.g. right before `const (\n\t// Version of Echo`):

```go
// RouteNotFound is special method name used to register a route that is executed when no other route matches
const RouteNotFound = "echo_route_not_found"
```

2) /echo/echo.go — add this method next to the other route-registration methods (e.g. right after `func (e *Echo) Any(...)`):

```go
// RouteNotFound registers a special-case route which is executed when no other route is found (i.e. HTTP 404 cases)
// for current host and method. `Echo#RouteNotFound()` can be used for routes that should be matched only when no
// other route matches.
func (e *Echo) RouteNotFound(path string, h HandlerFunc, m ...MiddlewareFunc) *Route {
	return e.Add(RouteNotFound, path, h, m...)
}
```

3) /echo/router.go — add a `routeNotFound HandlerFunc` field to the `methodHandler` struct; in `func (n *node) addHandler(method string, h HandlerFunc)` add `case RouteNotFound:\n\t\tn.methodHandler.routeNotFound = h`; in `func (n *node) findHandler(method string) HandlerFunc` add `case RouteNotFound:\n\t\treturn n.methodHandler.routeNotFound`.
